finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a caller-supplied URL. Its only check is `urlparse(url).hostname.endswith("example.com")`. That check has no leading dot, so any domain ending in the string `example.com` passes, for example `attackerexample.com` or `evil-example.com`. The unused constant ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com" shows the dot was intended. The check is also a hostname-string check made before DNS resolution. An attacker-owned domain can therefore resolve to 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 or an RFC1918 address, and DNS rebinding works too. The scheme and port are not restricted. The validator uses urlparse and the fetcher uses httpx's own parser, and the original string is passed to the fetcher, so a parser-differential bypass is also possible. Impact is limited to a blind or semi-blind SSRF: only `len(r.text)`, an error, and timing are returned. That is enough for internal port and host scanning and for hitting internal GET endpoints. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so redirect-based bypasses do not apply.
finding.source: Query parameter `url` of GET /mirror (FastAPI `url: str`), fully attacker-controlled

trace.note: `url` is taken directly from the query string
host = urlparse(url).hostname or "" (urlparse parser, not httpx's)
Weak check: host.endswith("example.com") with no dot boundary. `attackerexample.com` passes. Hostname-string only, no resolved-IP check.
The original unmodified `url` string is fetched by httpx; the response length is returned at line 17

finding.guards_checked: Checked the endswith("example.com") hostname check: no dot boundary, so it is bypassable by registering a domain such as `evilexample.com` and pointing it at an internal IP. It does not resolve or validate the IP, so it is rebinding-prone. It does not check the scheme or port. The ALLOWED_SUFFIX constant is unused. There is no authentication, no egress filtering, and no IP blocklist or allowlist in the code. httpx follows redirects only when follow_redirects=True, and that is not set. The /ping endpoint (line 23) fetches a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: Only `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13 (suffix check, no dot boundary, no scheme/port/IP validation); no auth or middleware exists in the code, and mirror.py is the only file.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled and goes to `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16 after only the bypassable `endswith("example.com")` check at mirror.py:13, so `attackerexample.com` passes.
